name: ClinicBench
intro: ClinicBench是牛津大学和哈佛大学联合发布的临床场景大模型评测基准，涵盖临床语言生成、理解和推理等11个任务，引入了六个新数据集和复杂临床任务，全面评估LLM的临床能力。
org: University of Oxford, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
build_method: 整合11个已有临床数据集，并从MIMIC、ChatDoctor、DrugBank和Drugs.com构建6个经专家复核的新数据集
task_type: 多选题, 问答, 摘要, 实体识别, 关系抽取, 分类
eval_feature: 评估LLM在复杂临床问题解决, 临床语言理解, 生成和推理方面的能力
scale: 3类场景、11个任务、17个数据集、超过20,000个测试样本
task_type_en: Multiple choice, Q&A, Summarization, Named Entity Recognition, Relation Extraction, Classification
build_method_en: Combining existing datasets and constructing six new datasets, GPT-4 generated and expert reviewed
eval_feature_en: Evaluating LLM capabilities in complex clinical problem solving, clinical language understanding, generation, and reasoning
intro_en: ClinicBench, jointly released by Oxford University and Harvard University, is a clinical scenario large model evaluation benchmark covering 11 tasks including clinical language generation, understanding, and reasoning. It introduces six new datasets and complex clinical tasks to comprehensively assess the clinical capabilities of LLMs.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2405.00716. The paper defines ClinicBench as a comprehensive clinical benchmark with three scenarios, eleven tasks, and seventeen datasets spanning clinical language reasoning, generation, and understanding. It combines existing datasets for exam-style QA, radiology report summarization, named entity recognition, relation extraction, and document classification with six new complex clinical tasks. New datasets are derived from MIMIC-IV referral letters, ChatDoctor patient-physician conversations, MIMIC-IV EHRs, MIMIC-III health documents, DrugBank emerging drugs, and Drugs.com interaction data; GPT-4 generation is used for some QA creation and expert review, correction, and filtering are applied. The evaluation panel covers 22 LLMs, including 11 general and 11 medical models, across commercial and open-source systems. Results are reported under zero-shot and 1/3/5-shot settings with task-specific automatic metrics such as Accuracy, Micro F1, entity-level F1, and ROUGE-L. Clinical usefulness is separately assessed by three medical experts on hospitalization summarization and patient education samples using factuality, completeness, preference, and safety criteria.
